MUTUAL CONFIDENTIALITY AGREEMENT

1. Purpose and parties
ExampleCorp Ltd and Brackenridge Systems, each a company incorporated in England and Wales and identified in the signature block below, enter into this mutual confidentiality agreement so that both sides can exchange sensitive material while they decide whether to pursue a commercial relationship. In this document, each company is referred to separately as a party and jointly as the parties.

2. Meaning of Confidential Information
For the purposes of this agreement, Confidential Information covers anything one party shares with the other, in whatever form, where the material is labelled as confidential or where a reasonable person would treat it as confidential because of what it is and the circumstances in which it was shared. It includes, among other things, technical material, product roadmaps, pricing, financial figures, business strategy, and customer or supplier details, and it makes no difference whether the sharing happened before or after this agreement was signed.

3. Keeping information confidential
Each party undertakes to hold the other party's Confidential Information in strict confidence, to put it to no use other than assessing a possible business relationship, and to safeguard it with no less care than it applies to its own sensitive material, and always with at least reasonable care. Neither party may pass the other party's Confidential Information to any outside person except in the ways this agreement allows, and each party answers for the conduct of every person to whom it passes that material under this agreement.

4. Sharing that is allowed
A party is permitted to share Confidential Information with members of its staff, its professional advisers, and its group companies, but only where those recipients genuinely need the material for the assessment described above and are themselves bound by confidentiality duties no weaker than the duties set out here. A party may also hand over Confidential Information where a statute, a regulation, or a competent court compels it to do so, provided that it alerts the other party in writing as soon as it is able, whenever the law permits that, and confines what it hands over to the portion it is legally obliged to reveal.

5. Handing back or destroying information
If either party asks the other in writing, the party receiving the request must, without delay, give back or wipe out every item of the requesting party's Confidential Information that it holds or controls, and must confirm the destruction in writing if asked to do so. Material that must be retained because the law requires it, or that sits in routine electronic backups, may be kept, but it remains protected by this agreement for as long as it is retained.

6. How long this agreement lasts
This agreement begins on the day the second of the two signatures is added to it and runs for two (2) years from that day, unless it is brought to an end sooner in the manner described below. The parties may agree in writing, signed by both of them, to extend the agreement for a further period.

7. Ending the agreement early
Either party may bring this agreement to an end by giving the other party written notice at least thirty (30) days in advance. Ending the agreement early leaves untouched any rights or duties that had already built up before the end date, and the duty to keep information confidential carries on for three (3) years after the agreement comes to an end.

8. Limits on liability
The most either party can ever be liable for under this agreement is an amount equal to the fees that were paid or that fell due in the twelve months immediately before the event giving rise to the claim. Nothing in this agreement restricts any liability that the law does not allow to be restricted.

9. Which law applies
The law of England and Wales governs this agreement, and any dispute connected with it falls within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.

10. How to send formal notices
Any formal notice under this agreement must be made in writing and takes effect once it is delivered to the registered office of the party receiving it, addressed for the attention of its legal counsel. Delivery may be made by hand, by prepaid first-class post, or by email supported by confirmation of transmission.

11. Final points
This document represents the whole agreement between the parties on its subject matter and replaces all earlier conversations and understandings; any change to it is valid only if recorded in writing and signed by both parties. Should any part of this agreement be found invalid or unenforceable, the remainder continues to apply in full. A right under this agreement is not waived merely because a party is slow to enforce it, and this agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which counts as an original.
